fields.label: 시작 / 재개 checkpoint
fields.help: DAgger checkpoint to start from

fields.label: 맵 / 장애물 배치
fields.help: 'train' / 'heldout' / 'heldout_obstacles' / 'heldout_all', or a comma separated list in either grammar: 'real/bb22-1@rev#line:44' (new) or 'real:blackbox2022_1+rlobs44~rev' (loader). An open seed -- 'real/bb22-1#line:*' -- is drawn --obstacle-draws times.

fields.label: 맵별 장애물 배치 수
fields.help: how many random obstacle placements a '#<kind>:*' entry becomes. The draw comes from --seed, so the same seed gives the same maps, and the concrete names are recorded in the run manifest.

fields.label: 시뮬레이터 실행 방식
fields.help: simulator runtime. 'compile' is the current default and what every run so far used (torch.compile on the physics substep loop and the plan solver). 'eager' turns both off. 'graphs' turns both off and captures explicit CUDA graphs instead, which starts in about a second rather than minutes. Opt in only; nothing about the default changes.

fields.label: W&B 그룹
fields.help: W&B group. The pilot's arms share one so they can be read together.

fields.label: dial margin (학습 중 무작위 하향폭)
fields.help: --cond dial: the dial is the floor's friction minus a per-episode margin in [0, this]

fields.label: dial 을 정확히 알려줄 비율
fields.help: --cond dial: share of episodes with no margin

fields.label: grip budget penalty (dial 초과)
fields.help: --cond dial: per second, per (m/s^2)^2 of lateral acceleration beyond what the dial allows. This is what makes the dial a command under RL. A dial is a lower bound on the floor's grip, so return alone teaches the policy to drive faster than it was told; with the budget charged, what is optimised is the lap *inside* the dial

fields.label: raceline 목적함수
fields.help: line behind the lap-time reference and the teacher-driven opponents (default min_curvature)

fields.label: teacher 횡가속 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] lateral limit of that line's speed profile (default 6)

fields.label: teacher 구동가속 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] drive limit (default 6)

fields.label: teacher 제동 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] braking limit (default 3)

fields.label: friction conditioning (--cond)
fields.help: Stage-1 friction conditioning arm. 'none' is the unmodified policy; 'zero' (A0) and 'true_mu' (A1) both add the zero-initialised conditioning projection and differ only in what is fed to it. 'true_mu' is a LAB ORACLE: its input is privileged and its checkpoint refuses to load in the viewer, export, watch, evaluate or the ROS node.

fields.label: fresh optimizer 로 시작
fields.help: start Adam from scratch instead of restoring the checkpoint's moments. Required for the conditioning arms: adding a parameter shifts the positional keys Adam's state is indexed by, and silently re-keying them would give the two arms different optimiser state.

fields.label: controller adaptation
fields.help: D3 recurrent auto-controller adaptation stage; off preserves ordinary PPO

fields.label: 원본 D3 reference policy
fields.help: immutable original D3 checkpoint for recurrent KL; inherited on resume

fields.label: reference KL 적용 범위
fields.help: reference KL dimensions (adaptive default: curvature only)

fields.label: 연구용 미승인 estimator 허용
fields.help: explicitly train with an unapproved estimator candidate

fields.label: 학습 제어기
fields.help: controller arm between the policy and the wheels. 'legacy' is the untouched path and is the default, so an unflagged run is unchanged. 'fixed_low' is the control arm, 'oracle' reads the true friction (lab only), 'estimated' uses the frozen estimator's filtered lower quantile from causal sensors. A '+tcs' suffix (or 'tcs' alone) additionally runs the car's own traction guard on the speed command, fed from the simulated ERPM odometry and IMU; it needs vehicle.wheel_model. 'fixed_low+tcs' is the deployment default.

fields.label: grip estimator
fields.help: frozen grip-estimator checkpoint. Required by --controller estimated, and rejected for every other arm.

fields.label: critic privileged adapter
fields.help: declared privileged-input adapter for the critic, e.g. 'absent_opponent_17_to_21' to run a race-trained critic in a solo env. Empty is strict legacy.

fields.label: KL 감소 step
fields.help: env steps over which the imitation-KL leash decays to zero (default: --total, so it decays across the whole run). Shortening it to 20 %% was tried and reverted: on a 20M run the policy was clean while the leash held (collision rate 0.00, lap 17.4 s) and then traded safety for speed the moment it reached zero at 4M (0.33-0.47, lap 12.5 s), with KL to the imitation policy rising 0.26 -> 6.8. The leash was holding a speed/safety balance the reward alone does not

fields.label: critic warmup update
fields.help: updates with the actor frozen

fields.label: 로그 주기
fields.help: updates between W&B rows (1 = every update)

fields.label: mixed precision (bf16)
fields.help: bf16 autocast for network forward/backward (~2x faster)

fields.label: progress reward (m당)
fields.help: reward per metre of signed forward progress

fields.label: alive reward (제어 step당)
fields.help: constant reward per control step

fields.label: 벽 근접 penalty
fields.help: per-metre penalty at zero wall gap (0 = off)

fields.label: 벽 안전 거리 (m)
fields.help: [m] body-to-wall gap where the proximity penalty starts

fields.label: 역주행 penalty
fields.help: per-step penalty while facing backwards along the lane

fields.label: 충돌 속도 penalty
fields.help: extra collision penalty per m/s of impact speed

fields.label: speed cap 증가 충돌 기준
fields.help: >0: [collisions/km] the speed cap only rises while the recent crash rate is below this (safety before speed). Per km, not per episode: the fraction of episodes that end in a crash saturates at 1.0 as soon as episodes are long enough to almost always contain one, and a gate reading a saturated number can never open again no matter how much the policy improves

fields.label: speed cap 증가 평가 분위수
fields.help: which track holds the gate shut: 1.0 the worst, 0.9 the 90th percentile, 0.5 the median. The set average is what let a 12 coll/km map hide behind a 2.1 coll/km mean; the outright worst lets one pathological map freeze the curriculum for the other 148

fields.label: speed cap 증가 최소 평가 거리 (km)
fields.help: a track needs this many km driven before it can hold the gate shut. Distance, not episodes: it is what a rate per km is estimated from, and with 149 tracks sharing 1024 envs an episode count large enough to be meaningful takes longer to reach than the whole curriculum

fields.label: 근접 penalty 속도 기준 (m/s)
fields.help: [m/s] scale the proximity penalty by (1 + v/ref)

fields.label: plan 여유 penalty
fields.help: per-second penalty for a plan inside the wall margin

fields.label: 랩타임 bonus
fields.help: scale of the per-sector time reward. Progress already points at lap time, but shaving 0.1 s off a 13.5 s lap moves the return by under 1 %% -- and less the longer the track -- so the thing being optimised is nearly invisible to the optimiser. This term scores each sector against the track's own recent pace, in fractions of the headroom left to the raceline, so a hundredth found near the limit outweighs a tenth found far from it. At 2.0, and 1.5 s off the pace, 0.1 s of lap is worth about 0.8 against 80 for a collision; at 0.1 s off the pace a hundredth is worth 1.3

fields.label: W&B 재개 ID
fields.help: append to this W&B run id (default: the one the --init checkpoint came from)

fields.label: 새 W&B 실행 생성
fields.help: start a fresh W&B run even when resuming

fields.label: 지표 JSONL 출력 파일
fields.help: also append every logged metric dict to this file, one JSON object per logged update. Opt-in and orthogonal to --wandb: a `--wandb disabled` run otherwise leaves no machine-readable curve behind, which is exactly what a smoke has to report

fields.label: 재개 누적 step 기준
fields.help: x-axis offset for the resumed W&B run; defaults to the checkpoint's own count

fields.label: 시각화 실행 중 GPU 양보 비율
fields.help: while a viewer is on screen, sleep this multiple of each update's duration so it can reach the GPU. 1.0 halves the training rate and gives the viewer a usable frame rate; 0 disables it

fields.label: 추월 bonus
fields.help: reward per metre of arc taken out of the nearest opponent ahead. Needs --race-size > 1. Without it a collision penalty teaches avoidance and only avoidance: sitting behind costs nothing, so there is never a reason to pass

fields.label: 상대차 안전 간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] body gap below which the car proximity penalty starts. Larger = the policy is asked to react earlier when a door is closing

fields.label: sideslip (슬립각) penalty
fields.help: per metre driven, per radian of sideslip beyond ~3.5 deg: prices the grip limit itself instead of only the wall it ends at

fields.label: aux head · 상대차 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss making the actor's trunk predict the nearest opponent's offset and closing speed from the scan stack (races only). 0 = off

fields.label: aux head · 노면 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss making the actor's trunk predict the car's true friction from what it observes (IMU history). 0 = off

fields.label: aux head · 미래 예측 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss making the actor's RECURRENT STATE (the trunk features with --memory off) predict, 20 control steps (0.50 s) ahead: the nearest opponent's relative position and velocity in the ego frame, a presence logit, and the ego's own speed and yaw rate. Privileged labels from the simulator, masked across episode boundaries and where no opponent is in range. 0 = off, and off the head is not built at all: same parameters, same state dict, same loss. Measure what it did with `python -m f1sim.learn.probe_hidden`

fields.label: aux head · 미래 예측 step 수
fields.help: lookahead of --aux-future in control steps (40 Hz). Default 20 = 0.5 s. Only the last k steps of each --horizon chunk go unlabelled, so a k near the horizon leaves almost nothing to train on

fields.label: aux head · 노면 자세 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss making the actor's SCAN STEM predict, per beam, whether a return is the floor or a solid object. The label is free in the simulator (`scan_type == HIT_GROUND`); beams with no return are excluded. Weighted BCE, positive weight from the batch rate, recall AND precision reported every update. Never exported, off by default and byte-identical off. Needs --scan-stem resnet

fields.label: aux head · 노면 자세 폭
fields.help: channels in the per-beam floor head (--aux-floor)

fields.label: aux head · 미래 예측 폭
fields.help: hidden width of the future head's one layer

fields.label: TTC penalty
fields.help: per-step penalty at zero time to contact with the nearest car, ramping linearly from 0 at --ttc-safe. The reward audit (docs/research/reward-audit-2026-09-13.md) found nothing prices the *approach* to another car: car_proximity is charged per metre driven and only inside --car-safe-gap, so closing at 3 m/s from 2 m away -- 0.7 s from a contact -- costs zero. 0 = off.

fields.label: TTC 기준 (s)
fields.help: [s] time to contact above which --ttc-penalty is 0

fields.label: 선두 유지 거리 · 시간 · bonus
fields.help: pay BONUS once when the learner has led an opponent by DIST_M metres along the lane for TIME_S seconds continuously (1.5 1.0 <bonus> is the contract's default). Unlike --overtake-bonus, which pays dense arc gained and so pays the approach and the crossing instant, this pays only a pass that stuck.

fields.label: 상대차 상태 입력
fields.help: ORACLE. Append the simulator's own description of the nearest two opponents to the observation (f1sim/opp_token.py): 'pos' = relative position + presence, 'posvel' = + relative velocity, 'future' = + where each opponent's own controller intends to be at 0.10/0.25/0.50/0.75 s. The checkpoint records it and is refused by the exporter and the ROS node. Its purpose is to answer whether the planner, handed the opponent's state, races better than it does with LiDAR alone -- not to produce a policy.

fields.label: 모듈별 이름 기반 재초기화
fields.help: make two arms that differ by an input width differ by that alone. Re-initialises every tensor a warm start leaves fresh from its own module name rather than from the ambient generator (learn.model.reinit_fresh_by_name, from branch feat/motion-memory) -- otherwise the wider layer consumes different draws and every module built after it differs too -- and re-seeds the generator once the model is built, so the arms' exploration streams start identical as well.

fields.label: 상대차 근접 penalty
fields.help: per metre driven with another car's body inside car_safe_gap (0.6 m), scaled by closing speed. Without it the only gradient near a car is the overtake term paying for closing, right down to contact

fields.label: 상대차 접촉 penalty
fields.help: extra penalty for touching another car, on top of ending the episode. Contact and a wall otherwise score the same, so nothing tells the policy that a car is something to negotiate with rather than more scenery

fields.label: 완주 bonus
fields.help: reward per completed lap, multiplied by that lap's average speed (track length / lap time). Dense progress reward already stands in for lap time, but it saturates where the speed cap and not the corner sets the speed -- at a 4 m/s cap that is ~80 %% of these tracks, and there every path scores the same. This term keeps paying for a faster lap

fields.label: 초기 action log_std
fields.help: reset the actor's exploration log-std at start (default: -1.8 in the plan space, whose curvature knots tolerate far less noise than steer/speed; unchanged otherwise)

fields.label: LiDAR frame 간격
fields.help: control steps between stacked scans

fields.label: 차량 상태 이력 길이
fields.help: proprio history rows in the observation (20 = the last second at stride 2)

fields.label: 레이스당 차량 수
fields.help: cars per track instance (>1: opponents in the LiDAR, car-car collisions)

fields.label: 상대차 기본 종류
fields.help: who drives cars 1..M-1: the policy (self-play), the raceline teacher, per race one or the other (mixed, share set by --mixed-teacher-frac), or per race one entry drawn from --opp-pool (pool)

fields.label: 상대차 속도 배율 범위
fields.help: teacher opponents: speed scale range per race

fields.label: 상대 policy pool
fields.help: comma-separated opponent population for --opponent pool: checkpoint paths, 'self' (the learner's own current weights, i.e. self-play) and 'teacher' (the raceline teacher, carrying --opp-events). One entry is drawn per race from the simulator's generator. Empty = off. A checkpoint is the only opponent that takes its own line, defends its own position and makes its own mistakes; every scripted behaviour is still the same tracker on the same line being told what to do

fields.label: 출발 종방향 간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] arc along the lane between the cars of a race at spawn, drawn uniformly per reset. The default is the range every race so far was trained at, so an unflagged run is unchanged. Widening it is an opponent-diversity axis: a fixed narrow band shows the policy one approach geometry

fields.label: 학습 차량 출발 위치
fields.help: where the learner starts on the grid of a race whose other cars are not itself: behind (every race trained so far -- a pass to make), ahead (a place to defend, and the only way to be overtaken), alongside (side by side, which is where the contacts measured in traffic actually happen) or random (drawn per race)

fields.label: 나란한 차량 횡간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] body-to-body lateral gap asked for on an alongside grid; what the lane has room for wins, and a lane with room for one car spawns a stagger

fields.label: 나란한 차량 종간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] arc stagger inside an alongside grid, drawn independently per car. Small on purpose: a grid's lateral offsets are taken along the centerline normal at each car's own arc position, and those normals stop agreeing a few tens of centimetres apart on a tight corner

fields.label: 상대차 행동 event
fields.help: comma-separated behaviour for the teacher-driven opponents. Timed events (brake,stop,shift,weave) fire at --opp-event-rate; reactive behaviours (defend,yield,line,oblivious) read the learner's position every step and each takes its own --opp-<name>-prob. Empty = off. A teacher opponent otherwise only ever presents a slower car on the racing line, which is the one overtaking and avoidance problem the policy has already been trained on

fields.label: 상대차 event 빈도 (10s당)
fields.help: expected timed events per teacher opponent per 10 s of driving (events do not overlap, so the realized rate is a little below this)

fields.label: opp brake scale
fields.help: brake: fraction of its profile speed the opponent drops to

fields.label: opp brake time
fields.help: [s] how long a brake event holds

fields.label: opp stop time
fields.help: [s] how long a stopped opponent stays stopped

fields.label: opp shift offset
fields.help: [m] |lateral offset| of a lane change; the sign is drawn separately

fields.label: opp shift hold
fields.help: [s] time held at the offset, between the ramp in and the ramp out

fields.label: opp shift ramp
fields.help: [s] ramp in / ramp out of a shift

fields.label: opp weave amp
fields.help: [m] sinusoidal lateral amplitude of a weave

fields.label: opp weave period
fields.help: [s] weave period

fields.label: opp weave time
fields.help: [s] how long a weave lasts

fields.label: opp event margin
fields.help: [m] free space kept beyond the car's half-width when an event moves an opponent off the raceline; the offset is clamped per raceline point against the track's distance field, so it can never reach a wall

fields.label: opp defend prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent defends): while a learner is within --opp-defend-range behind, it moves its line toward the side that learner is coming down, at full amplitude inside --opp-defend-full

fields.label: opp yield prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent yields): with a learner alongside it moves away

fields.label: opp line prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent drives its own corner line): an out-in or in-out offset sweep, drawn per corner

fields.label: opp oblivious prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent's follow-gap slowdown is off): it does not brake for a car ahead or beside it. This is the car that rams -- the situation the training distribution has never contained on purpose

fields.label: opp defend offset
fields.help: [m] how far across a defending opponent moves, drawn per race

fields.label: opp yield offset
fields.help: [m] ... a yielding one

fields.label: opp line offset
fields.help: [m] ... each end of a corner-line sweep, drawn per corner

fields.label: opp defend range
fields.help: [m] how far behind a learner starts being defended against; 0 = the env's own overtake_range (12 m), the window the overtake reward calls a race

fields.label: opp defend full
fields.help: [m] inside this the block is at full amplitude, ramping to zero at --opp-defend-range

fields.label: opp alongside lon
fields.help: [m] |longitudinal offset| within which two cars count as alongside (bodies are 0.58 m long). Read by `yield` and by the census, which must measure the situation the behaviour reacts to

fields.label: opp alongside lat
fields.help: [m] ... and the lateral bound, so a car across a hairpin is not alongside

fields.label: opp react max
fields.help: [m] cap on the reactive lateral offset, before the lane's own clamp

fields.label: opp react slew
fields.help: [m/s] rate limit on it: a target that jumps sideways asks the pure-pursuit teacher for a step steer input

fields.label: opp corner kappa
fields.help: [1/m] smoothed raceline curvature above which a point is in a corner, for the `line` behaviour

fields.label: opp corner min arc
fields.help: [m] shortest run of such points that counts as one corner

fields.label: opp corner smooth
fields.help: [m] window the curvature is averaged over first

fields.label: 차량별 상대차 설정
fields.help: per-opponent configuration: a JSON array with one object per car of a race (race_size - 1 of them), or @path/to/slots.json. Each object may carry kind (raceline|interactive|forzaeth|forzaeth_pred|lane_switch|layout|policy|self), kind_mix (several teacher kinds, one drawn per race reset -- how one run sees every driver instead of one), checkpoint, controller, speed_scale (a number or [lo, hi]), label_grip (true|nominal|conservative), speed_cap [m/s], events (brake,stop,shift,weave), event_rate, reactive ({defend: p,yield: p,line: p,oblivious: p}), spawn (ahead|behind|alongside|random, where that car starts relative to the learner) and seed. Slot i of every race in the batch is built from spec i, so 'a slow car ahead and a defending car alongside' is one run rather than two. Replaces --opponent / --opp-speed / --opp-pool / --opp-events / --spawn-order, which say one thing about every opponent at once; the remaining --opp-* flags are the shared *ranges* an event draws from and still apply. Empty = off, and off is the env this flag was added to

fields.label: action space
fields.help: plan: the policy outputs a local trajectory (f1sim.mpc)

fields.label: policy memory
fields.help: give the actor (and by default the critic) a recurrent memory over the per-step trunk embedding, warm-started from --init so that step 0 is bit-identical to it. 'off' is the untouched run in every respect: same network, same rollout, same minibatching, same loss. The six-frame stack stays the input; this extends the window past the 150 ms it covers, which is what a box that has left the scan cannot otherwise survive

fields.label: policy GRU hidden 크기
fields.help: GRU width (<= 256, the contract's ceiling). 128 over the 384-wide trunk embedding measures at 1.07x the frozen actor's CPU forward time against a 1.5x budget; see `python -m f1sim.learn.budget`

fields.label: critic memory
fields.help: 'own' gives the critic its own GRU (it already has its own stem, and it reads the privileged vector the actor must never see, so sharing the recurrence would be the one place a value gradient reached the actor's trunk). 'none' leaves the critic feedforward

fields.label: LiDAR 추가 channel
fields.help: comma separated extra scan channels, off by default (memory,edges,aligned,aligned_prev,aligned_valid,floor,fe_floor,fe_range). 'memory': the closest return seen at each bearing in the last --scan-memory-tau seconds, decayed -- explicit cheap memory the GRU does not have to learn. 'edges': |r[i]-r[i-1]| per beam, so the crack between two boxes in a row reads as two discontinuities rather than an opening. 'floor': the per-beam likelihood that a return is the FLOOR rather than a solid object, from the beam geometry and an attitude tracked off the IMU the observation already carries (`learn/floor.py`); 0 = solid, 1 = floor, 0.5 = the attitude is not usable. 'fe_floor' / 'fe_range': the same two quantities read off the trained sensor front-end (--frontend) instead of the geometry. 'aligned': the signed residual between this scan and the one from --aligned-k steps ago warped into the current ego frame with the car's OWN measured speed, yaw rate and roll/pitch -- static geometry cancels and what moved by itself is what is left (learn.aligned). It is the one channel with a gate, because the tilt is measured rather than known. All of them are arithmetic on what the env already emits and all start as zeroed input columns, so a warm start is still bit-identical

fields.label: aligned k
fields.help: [aligned] control steps of lag the residual is taken over (4 = 100 ms)

fields.label: aligned tau
fields.help: [aligned] soft threshold: sign(R) * max(|R| - tau, 0). Fixed BEFORE training at 2-3 sigma of the static-world floor measured on the real bags (python -m f1sim.learn.aligned_floor), never tuned on a result

fields.label: aligned tau rel
fields.help: [aligned] range-proportional addition to tau (0 by default: the contract asks for one number)

fields.label: aligned tol beams
fields.help: [aligned] bearing uncertainty of the warp, in beams

fields.label: aligned consist beams
fields.help: [aligned] bearing tolerance of the two-frame consistency test, in beams

fields.label: aligned z tol
fields.help: [aligned] a warped point further than this out of the current scan plane is dropped as not comparable

fields.label: aligned gap fill
fields.help: [aligned] beams a hole left by the warp's resampling may be filled from

fields.label: motion memory 사용
fields.help: split the recurrent state: add a small GRU (--motion-hidden, <= 64) fed by an encoder of the ALIGNED rows only, whose output enters the actor's and critic's first MLP preactivation through its own zero-initialised projection. h_dyn is carried inside the same hidden tensor as the main state, so every path that carries one carries this too. Off = no module, no meta, no RNG draw

fields.label: motion GRU hidden 크기
fields.help: width of h_dyn. The contract caps it at 64: the claim under test is that the remedy is inductive bias rather than capacity

fields.label: motion channel
fields.help: output channels of the motion encoder's last convolution

fields.label: critic 에도 motion 적용
fields.help: 'own' gives the critic its own motion branch, as --memory-critic does

fields.label: aux head · 상대차 mask 가중치
fields.help: E3-a. Weighted BCE on a per-beam 'is this beam on another car' logit read from the MOTION ENCODER's features. The label is the LiDAR's own scan_type == HIT_CAR -- privileged, train-time, and already cast. The logits are never fed to the planner and never exported

fields.label: aux head · motion 가중치
fields.help: E3-b. MSE on the nearest opponent's CURRENT relative velocity, read from h_dyn alone. Masked by presence, like the future head's opponent columns

fields.label: scan memory 시간 (s)
fields.help: [s] time constant of the decayed scan-occupancy channel

fields.label: frontend checkpoint
fields.help: trained sensor front-end (`work/frontend/train.py`) for the `fe_floor` / `fe_range` scan channels. Frozen: it is a sensor model, not part of the policy, and PPO never sees a gradient through it

fields.label: 노면 자세 입력
fields.help: attitude source of the `floor` scan channel. 'ego' is `floor.EgoStateAttitude` -- the suspension's calibrated response to the accelerations the car itself produces, read off the wheel speed and the gyro's yaw, which is the most accurate of the three (measured). 'tracker' is `floor.AttitudeTracker`, gyro integration with the accelerometer gated on quiescence. 'vesc' is the orientation quaternion the ROS node reads today, which is wrong by 8 deg rms while driving and is here only so the comparison can be run

fields.label: LiDAR 시간 차분 입력
fields.help: append temporal scan differences for a new model without --init

fields.label: LiDAR encoder (scan stem)
fields.help: scan encoder for a new model without --init (an --init checkpoint keeps its own)

fields.label: 상대차 미래 예측
fields.help: which prediction the block's 'future' columns carry (f1sim.gym_env.OPP_FUTURE_MODELS); recorded in the spec, because the same columns under two models are two different inputs

fields.label: procedural 장애물 episode 비율
fields.help: share of env resets that get a freshly drawn obstacle layout, placed as analytic props from the hard-obstacle patterns (0 = off, and off is byte-identical to a run without the flag)

fields.label: plan kappa mode
fields.help: what a curvature knot of +-1 means: +-1.6 1/m ('absolute', every run before this) or the tightest arc the tyres hold at the plan's speed ('feasible'). At 5 m/s 'absolute' spends four fifths of the box on arcs the car cannot drive, and the policy's own exploration is wider than the band that is left.

fields.label: plan kappa a lat
fields.help: 'feasible' only: the lateral budget the knots are scaled by

fields.label: 장애물 밀도 (10m당)
fields.help: patterns per 10 m of lap when --procedural-obstacles is on

fields.label: 장애물 최대 개수
fields.help: prop slots per env (0: from the density and the longest lap). Every slot costs the beam tracer one pass per step, so this is the cost dial

fields.label: 장애물 raceline 여유 (m)
fields.help: [m] kept clear either side of the raceline, beyond the car's half-width, so the teacher opponents are never routed through a prop

fields.label: raceline 위 장애물 허용 (corridor off)
fields.help: whether that corridor is enforced at all. 'off' lets a layout stand ON the racing line, which is the only way the policy ever meets an obstacle there -- and it does not today. Requires --spawn-runway and every teacher-driven car to be a prop-aware kind (--opp-slots), because a raceline-driven opponent cannot see a prop and its crashes would become the collision rate

fields.label: 충돌 처리 (terminate / soft)
fields.help: what a collision is. 'terminate' ends the episode, which is what every number on record was measured under. 'soft' resolves the contact and carries on -- the car is pushed out of penetration, its into-surface velocity is taken, and the crash is charged as a cost. It is the only way a policy can learn what to do AFTER a touch: steer out of it, back off and go again, and above all not end up driving the wrong way (--wrong-way-penalty). Not comparable with a 'terminate' run's collisions per km without saying so

fields.label: algo
fields.help: the learning algorithm. 'sac': soft actor-critic with a replay buffer on the same environment, model and conditioning; the actor is the same module, so its checkpoints (sac_u*.pt) load wherever a PPO one does

fields.label: sac buffer
fields.help: replay capacity, learner transitions

fields.label: sac updates per step
fields.help: gradient steps per env step (an env step adds one transition per learner row)

fields.label: sac start
fields.help: transitions buffered before any update (the first thousands are all starts)

fields.label: sac critic warmup
fields.help: updates of the Q functions alone before the actor moves: they start as the PPO value function and know nothing yet about what an action does

fields.label: sac actor every
fields.help: one actor step per this many critic steps (delayed policy updates)

fields.label: sac target entropy
fields.help: default: the starting policy's own entropy, so the exploration it had is kept

fields.label: sac anchor
fields.help: weight of ||mu(s) - mu_init(s)||^2 in the actor loss at the start

fields.label: sac anchor decay
fields.help: learner steps over which the anchor decays linearly to zero

fields.label: sac contact frac
fields.help: share of each batch drawn from the half second before a wall/prop contact

fields.label: sac n step
fields.help: rewards summed before bootstrapping; 1 is plain one-step TD

fields.label: sac actor loss
fields.help: 'awac': advantage-weighted regression onto buffer actions (conservative, the default after sac1's reparameterised actor drove worse behind an unfitted Q); 'sac': the soft actor-critic update with a learned temperature

fields.label: kind mix assign
fields.help: how a kind_mix opponent slot picks its driver. 'partition' (training's default): race g drives kind_mix[g %% len], fixed -- every update holds each kind in exact proportion, and a teacher that can plan a subset plans only its own rows (the interactive opponent was half a graphed step planning all of them). 'redraw': uniformly at every race reset, as the console does and as spec_korea_contact_s911/s912 were trained

fields.label: 장애물이 밀림 (질량 있음)
fields.help: a struck obstacle is shoved instead of being a wall with a crate's shape: each carries the mass of what it is (cardboard box 1.2 kg, wooden crate 10, steel drum 18, against a 3.74 kg car) and a contact exchanges momentum both ways. Needs --collision-mode soft

fields.label: spawn 활주로 (m)
fields.help: [m] of clear road every spawning car is guaranteed ahead of it, prop or wall. 0 = off. A car is placed at up to the spawn speed and cannot stop inside v^2/2a plus its own length, so a crate nearer than that is a collision it was never given the chance to avoid -- and it lands in the collision rate, making the metric read worse the more interesting the layout is. About 3 m for the default spawn speed

fields.label: raceline 경계 여유 (m)
fields.help: [m] free space the opponents' raceline keeps from the boundary (default 0.40)

fields.label: teacher 마찰 정보
fields.help: grip the teacher opponents' speed profile assumes

fields.label: teacher 방향 복구 시간 (s)
fields.help: [s] >0: cap the teacher's commanded speed at what can still be steered back onto the lane (v <= a_lat * t / heading_error). 0 keeps the old behaviour, where a car facing backwards on the line is told to carry full racing speed

fields.label: 맵 / 장애물 배치
fields.help: 'train', 'eval' or comma separated catalog names

fields.label: 수집 step
fields.help: learner steps per iteration (x envs/race-size labels), split across solo/traffic when enabled

fields.label: 단독·무장애물 데이터 비율 (0.3 = 30%)
fields.help: 학습 차량이 수집한 Teacher 라벨 개수 기준입니다. 0.3은 약 30%를 상대차·배치 장애물 없는 환경에서 수집합니다. 스텝 반올림 후 실제 비율은 실행 기록에 남습니다.

fields.label: 단독 주행 맵 (비우면 선택한 맵의 장애물 제거)
fields.help: 비워 두면 위에서 선택한 맵을 사용합니다. 따로 지정한 맵도 배치 장애물을 모두 제거하고 상대차 없이 수집합니다.

fields.label: action space
fields.help: plan: the student outputs a local trajectory (f1sim.mpc)

fields.label: teacher 속도 배율
fields.help: scale on the teacher's speed profile (0.9: fewer teacher crashes through the plan tracker)

fields.label: 차량 상태 이력 길이
fields.help: proprio history rows in the observation

fields.label: LiDAR 시간 차분 입력
fields.help: append temporal scan differences before the CNN

fields.label: LiDAR encoder (scan stem)
fields.help: scan encoder: 'resnet' adds GroupNorm/residual blocks, a whole-scan receptive field, a beam-angle channel and a raw per-sector nearest-return bypass

fields.label: raceline 경계 여유 (m)
fields.help: [m] free space the teacher's raceline keeps from the boundary (default 0.40). A minimum-curvature line has no robustness budget: the teacher tracks it with ground-truth pose and latency compensation, the student has neither

fields.label: plan 속도 표현 (speed mode)
fields.help: what the plan's speed dimensions mean (f1sim.mpc.SPEED_MODES). 'linear': two speeds, linear between (every existing checkpoint). 'envelope': a grip belief a_hat and an end speed; the profile follows the plan's own curvature. 'knots': a speed at every curvature knot

fields.label: grip pinball τ
fields.help: envelope only: pinball-loss quantile for the grip-belief dimension. 0.5 is the plain Huber loss; below it, a student that cannot tell the floor yet assumes the slippery end

fields.label: friction conditioning (--cond)
fields.help: condition the student on friction (learn/conditioning.py). 'true_mu' is a LAB ORACLE: the input is privileged and does not exist on the car. It answers one question -- does a student that is *told* the floor drive it? 'dial' is the deployable form: the student is told the floor's friction minus a per-episode margin and the teacher drives for that same number, so the input is a command an operator or a supervisor sets

fields.label: dial margin (학습 중 무작위 하향폭)
fields.help: dial: largest margin below the true friction

fields.label: dial 을 정확히 알려줄 비율
fields.help: dial: share of episodes with no margin at all

fields.label: aux head · 노면 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss asking the actor's grip head for the env's friction, from the same features the action is read from

fields.label: aux head · 상대차 가중치
fields.help: weight of an auxiliary loss asking the actor's opponent head where the nearest car is and how fast it is closing. Needs --race-size > 1. The teacher never looks at an opponent, so it cannot demonstrate a pass or a yield -- but 'a car is there and it moves like this' is read out of how the LiDAR returns shift, and the simulator knows the answer

fields.label: BPTT 구간 길이 (step)
fields.help: train on contiguous runs of this many steps per env (needs --memory gru to matter). 0 = i.i.d. samples, which never contain both the corner that showed the grip and the next one

fields.label: BPTT warm-up step
fields.help: leading steps of each run that only warm the state up

fields.label: raceline 목적함수
fields.help: line the teacher follows: 'min_time' refines the minimum-curvature line by descending the lap time of the speed profile at the --teacher-a-* limits (default: min_curvature)

fields.label: teacher 횡가속 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] lateral limit of the teacher's speed profile (default 6.0)

fields.label: teacher 구동가속 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] drive limit of the profile (default 6.0)

fields.label: teacher 제동 한계 (m/s²)
fields.help: [m/s^2] braking limit of the profile (default 3.0)

fields.label: teacher 마찰 정보
fields.help: grip the teacher's speed profile assumes. 'true' is privileged, so identical scans get speed labels up to 2.2x apart and the Huber loss can only fit their mean

fields.label: teacher 방향 복구 시간 (s)
fields.help: [s] >0: cap the teacher's commanded speed at what can still be steered back onto the lane (v <= a_lat * t / heading_error). 0 keeps the old behaviour, where a car facing backwards on the line is told to carry full racing speed

fields.label: teacher 종류
fields.help: raceline: pure pursuit on the precomputed line, blind to the other cars (every DAgger run before this one). interactive: f1sim.interactive_teacher, which scores a family of plans against the opponents' predicted motion and labels with the argmin -- the only one of the two that can demonstrate a pass

fields.label: teacher 예측 시간 (s)
fields.help: [s] how far the interactive teacher rolls each candidate out and how far ahead it reads the opponents

fields.label: teacher 후보 개선 반복
fields.help: Gauss-Newton iterations per candidate plan (the reference plan uses 6; the fit starts from a pure-pursuit blend that is already close)

fields.label: teacher 횡방향 후보 (m)
fields.help: [m left of the raceline] the candidate family's lateral offsets

fields.label: teacher 속도 후보 배율
fields.help: multipliers on the plan's speed targets

fields.label: teacher cost 가중치 5종
fields.help: the five cost weights (f1sim.interactive_teacher.TeacherCost); empty = its defaults

fields.label: 상대차 상태 입력
fields.help: privileged opponent block in the observation. An ORACLE: the other cars' true relative position ('pos'), velocity ('posvel') and future ('future'), from the simulator. Refused by the exporter and by the ROS node; a checkpoint trained with it is a measurement, not a policy

fields.label: 상대차 미래 예측
fields.help: which prediction the 'future' columns and the interactive teacher read (f1sim.gym_env.OPP_FUTURE_MODELS)

fields.label: policy memory
fields.help: gru: a recurrent student, trained by truncated BPTT over --chunk-length steps

fields.label: LiDAR 추가 channel
fields.help: extra scan channels (memory,edges,aligned,aligned_prev,aligned_valid,floor,fe_floor,fe_range), as in ppo.py

fields.label: speed imitation loss
fields.help: loss on the plan's two SPEED targets (the curvature knots keep the Huber either way). 'symmetric' is the loss every DAgger run before this flag used and is byte-identical to it. 'asym' is quadratic above the teacher's speed and linear below it, in m/s: with a mu-dependent label a symmetric regression fits the conditional MEAN of speed labels that are 2.2x apart, which is too fast on exactly the low-grip draws where too fast ends the episode. The asymmetry moves that optimum to a low quantile, so a student that cannot resolve grip backs off and one that can still reaches the limit at zero loss. Constants: w_over 4, w_under 0.25, under power 1

fields.label: GRU chunk length
fields.help: truncated-BPTT length for a recurrent student. The buffer is (steps, envs), so a chunk is a slice of it; a recurrent policy trained one isolated step at a time is not the policy that drives

fields.label: 시작 / 재개 checkpoint
fields.help: warm start the student from this checkpoint. Memory, extra scan channels and the privileged opponent block are added by name with zeroed new columns, so the student starts as the checkpoint and learns to use what was added

fields.label: hard sample 비율
fields.help: fraction of each training batch drawn in proportion to the student-teacher gap at collection time. 0 = uniform (previous behaviour). Measured motivation: the student matches the teacher to within 2 %% on the teacher's own trajectory but is 4-10x further off in the second before a collision, and a uniform loss barely sees those states

fields.label: hard sample 가중 지수
fields.help: exponent on the gap when weighting

fields.label: DAgger 데이터 보관 반복 수
fields.help: aggregate the data of at most this many recent iterations (host RAM)

fields.label: DAgger 재개 반복 번호
fields.help: index of the first iteration to run. For RESUMING a killed run from its last checkpoint: beta, the exploration noise and the checkpoint names all key off the true iteration index, so restarting a run that died after iteration 6 needs --start-iter 7, not --iters 1 (which is iteration 0, where beta is 1.0 and the TEACHER drives). What it cannot restore is the aggregated buffer: DAgger trains on the last --keep-iters collections and those live in host RAM only, so a resumed iteration trains on its own data alone. Declare that wherever the run is reported.

fields.label: 로그 주기
fields.help: training steps between W&B loss rows (was 200)

fields.label: 평가 주기
fields.help: evaluate every Nth iteration (the last one always). 1 = every iteration, the old behaviour. The evaluation is a diagnostic and cannot reach the training data (see rng_island), so this trades diagnostic resolution for wall-clock and nothing else.

fields.label: 컴파일 없이 실행 (eager)
fields.help: disable simulator / tracker compilation (CPU smoke tests)

fields.label: 레이스당 차량 수
fields.help: cars per track instance (>1: opponents in the LiDAR, car-car collisions)

fields.label: 상대차 기본 종류
fields.help: who drives cars 1..M-1: the policy (self-play), the raceline teacher, per race one or the other (mixed, share set by --mixed-teacher-frac), or per race one entry drawn from --opp-pool (pool)

fields.label: 상대차 속도 배율 범위
fields.help: teacher opponents: speed scale range per race

fields.label: 상대 policy pool
fields.help: comma-separated opponent population for --opponent pool: checkpoint paths, 'self' (the learner's own current weights, i.e. self-play) and 'teacher' (the raceline teacher, carrying --opp-events). One entry is drawn per race from the simulator's generator. Empty = off. A checkpoint is the only opponent that takes its own line, defends its own position and makes its own mistakes; every scripted behaviour is still the same tracker on the same line being told what to do

fields.label: 출발 종방향 간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] arc along the lane between the cars of a race at spawn, drawn uniformly per reset. The default is the range every race so far was trained at, so an unflagged run is unchanged. Widening it is an opponent-diversity axis: a fixed narrow band shows the policy one approach geometry

fields.label: 학습 차량 출발 위치
fields.help: where the learner starts on the grid of a race whose other cars are not itself: behind (every race trained so far -- a pass to make), ahead (a place to defend, and the only way to be overtaken), alongside (side by side, which is where the contacts measured in traffic actually happen) or random (drawn per race)

fields.label: 나란한 차량 횡간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] body-to-body lateral gap asked for on an alongside grid; what the lane has room for wins, and a lane with room for one car spawns a stagger

fields.label: 나란한 차량 종간격 (m)
fields.help: [m] arc stagger inside an alongside grid, drawn independently per car. Small on purpose: a grid's lateral offsets are taken along the centerline normal at each car's own arc position, and those normals stop agreeing a few tens of centimetres apart on a tight corner

fields.label: 상대차 행동 event
fields.help: comma-separated behaviour for the teacher-driven opponents. Timed events (brake,stop,shift,weave) fire at --opp-event-rate; reactive behaviours (defend,yield,line,oblivious) read the learner's position every step and each takes its own --opp-<name>-prob. Empty = off. A teacher opponent otherwise only ever presents a slower car on the racing line, which is the one overtaking and avoidance problem the policy has already been trained on

fields.label: 상대차 event 빈도 (10s당)
fields.help: expected timed events per teacher opponent per 10 s of driving (events do not overlap, so the realized rate is a little below this)

fields.label: opp brake scale
fields.help: brake: fraction of its profile speed the opponent drops to

fields.label: opp brake time
fields.help: [s] how long a brake event holds

fields.label: opp stop time
fields.help: [s] how long a stopped opponent stays stopped

fields.label: opp shift offset
fields.help: [m] |lateral offset| of a lane change; the sign is drawn separately

fields.label: opp shift hold
fields.help: [s] time held at the offset, between the ramp in and the ramp out

fields.label: opp shift ramp
fields.help: [s] ramp in / ramp out of a shift

fields.label: opp weave amp
fields.help: [m] sinusoidal lateral amplitude of a weave

fields.label: opp weave period
fields.help: [s] weave period

fields.label: opp weave time
fields.help: [s] how long a weave lasts

fields.label: opp event margin
fields.help: [m] free space kept beyond the car's half-width when an event moves an opponent off the raceline; the offset is clamped per raceline point against the track's distance field, so it can never reach a wall

fields.label: opp defend prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent defends): while a learner is within --opp-defend-range behind, it moves its line toward the side that learner is coming down, at full amplitude inside --opp-defend-full

fields.label: opp yield prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent yields): with a learner alongside it moves away

fields.label: opp line prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent drives its own corner line): an out-in or in-out offset sweep, drawn per corner

fields.label: opp oblivious prob
fields.help: P(a teacher-driven opponent's follow-gap slowdown is off): it does not brake for a car ahead or beside it. This is the car that rams -- the situation the training distribution has never contained on purpose

fields.label: opp defend offset
fields.help: [m] how far across a defending opponent moves, drawn per race

fields.label: opp yield offset
fields.help: [m] ... a yielding one

fields.label: opp line offset
fields.help: [m] ... each end of a corner-line sweep, drawn per corner

fields.label: opp defend range
fields.help: [m] how far behind a learner starts being defended against; 0 = the env's own overtake_range (12 m), the window the overtake reward calls a race

fields.label: opp defend full
fields.help: [m] inside this the block is at full amplitude, ramping to zero at --opp-defend-range

fields.label: opp alongside lon
fields.help: [m] |longitudinal offset| within which two cars count as alongside (bodies are 0.58 m long). Read by `yield` and by the census, which must measure the situation the behaviour reacts to

fields.label: opp alongside lat
fields.help: [m] ... and the lateral bound, so a car across a hairpin is not alongside

fields.label: opp react max
fields.help: [m] cap on the reactive lateral offset, before the lane's own clamp

fields.label: opp react slew
fields.help: [m/s] rate limit on it: a target that jumps sideways asks the pure-pursuit teacher for a step steer input

fields.label: opp corner kappa
fields.help: [1/m] smoothed raceline curvature above which a point is in a corner, for the `line` behaviour

fields.label: opp corner min arc
fields.help: [m] shortest run of such points that counts as one corner

fields.label: opp corner smooth
fields.help: [m] window the curvature is averaged over first

fields.label: 차량별 상대차 설정
fields.help: per-opponent configuration: a JSON array with one object per car of a race (race_size - 1 of them), or @path/to/slots.json. Each object may carry kind (raceline|interactive|forzaeth|forzaeth_pred|lane_switch|layout|policy|self), kind_mix (several teacher kinds, one drawn per race reset -- how one run sees every driver instead of one), checkpoint, controller, speed_scale (a number or [lo, hi]), label_grip (true|nominal|conservative), speed_cap [m/s], events (brake,stop,shift,weave), event_rate, reactive ({defend: p,yield: p,line: p,oblivious: p}), spawn (ahead|behind|alongside|random, where that car starts relative to the learner) and seed. Slot i of every race in the batch is built from spec i, so 'a slow car ahead and a defending car alongside' is one run rather than two. Replaces --opponent / --opp-speed / --opp-pool / --opp-events / --spawn-order, which say one thing about every opponent at once; the remaining --opp-* flags are the shared *ranges* an event draws from and still apply. Empty = off, and off is the env this flag was added to

fields.label: 초기 grip estimator (이어받기)
fields.help: optional compatible adaptive estimator weights; current CAL calibration is refitted

fields.label: TRAIN replay 데이터
fields.help: optional controlled TRAIN-only canonical sensor/target tensor dictionary; never CAL/DEV/FINAL

fields.label: 학습 batch 의 replay 비율
fields.help: replay share per minibatch in (0,1), rounded to rows; requires --replay-data when changed
